title: Improved classical optimization of fermionic Hamiltonians beyond Gaussian states
abstract: We give a polynomial-time randomized classical algorithm that approximates the largest eigenvalue $λ_{\max}$ of a traceless quartic fermionic Hamiltonian $H$ on $n$ modes. The algorithm achieves energy at least $λ_{\max}/O(\sqrt n)$ and outputs either a fermionic Gaussian state or a polynomially sparse state in the Fock basis. This is achieved through a new upper bound on $λ_{\max}$ in terms of the maximum energy of a Gaussian state and $\sqrt{2^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}(H^2)}$.
summary: This paper develops a polynomial-time classical algorithm to approximate the largest eigenvalue of a quartic fermionic Hamiltonian. It achieves this by establishing a rigorous upper bound that combines Gaussian expectations with sparse Fock-basis expectations. This improves the state-of-the-art approximation ratio for finding ground state energies in complex fermionic systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of finding the largest eigenvalue ($\lambda_{\max}$) of a complex, traceless quartic fermionic Hamiltonian ($H$) in polynomial time.
main_result: It presents a randomized classical algorithm that approximates $\lambda_{\max}(H)$ with an error bounded by $O(1/\sqrt{n})$, significantly improving upon previous bounds.
method: The approach combines two candidate states—a Gaussian state and a sparse Fock-basis state—by leveraging a key eigenvalue bound ($\lambda_{\max}(H) \le G(H) + 5\sqrt{n} \sigma$).
model_or_system: The system is an $n$-mode fermionic system described by a homogeneous quartic Hamiltonian $H$, involving Majorana operators. The analysis heavily relies on moment matrices and properties derived from Gaussian states.

important_parameters: The system size $n$, the normalized Frobenius norm $\sigma$, and the approximation error factors like $c_G \log(2n)$ and $\sqrt{n}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of moment matrix techniques and relies on bounding the difference between moment matrices of different states.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon establishing a crucial eigenvalue bound ($\lambda_{\max}(H) \le G(H) + 5\sqrt{n} \sigma$) by analyzing moment matrices, and then constructs a randomized algorithm that tests the two candidate states (Gaussian vs. sparse Fock-basis) derived from this bound.
why_interesting: The techniques developed—using moment matrix bounds and combining different state representations (Gaussian vs. sparse)—are highly relevant for optimizing ground state energies in strongly correlated fermionic models where exact diagonalization is intractable.
